TITLE: Newspaper headlines: 'Complete COP-out' and Fury's 'torment' - BBC News
DATES: ['2026-11-23T02:24:41.917Z', '2026-11-23T02:24:41.917Z']

BBC HomepageSkip to contentAccessibility HelpYour accountNotificationsHomeNewsSportWeatheriPlayerSoundsBitesizeCBBCCBeebiesFoodMore menuMore menuSearch BBCHomeNewsSportWeatheriPlayerSoundsBitesizeCBBCCBeebiesFoodClose menuBBC NewsMenuHomeUKWorldBusinessCulturePoliticsHealthTechInDepthBBC VerifyClimateMoreScienceFamily & EducationIn PicturesDisabilityNewsbeat'Complete COP-out' and Tyson Fury's 'torment'Published9 hours agoWarning: This paper review contains references to suicide

Image caption, The collapse of the COP31 climate talks in Turkey dominate Monday's front pages, with oil-rich countries being "accused of hijacking a deal to unite the world and fight climate change", according to the Metro. This year's UN climate summit was the most "chaotic" yet, the newspaper reports.

Image caption, The UK and EU rejected a COP31 pact that "failed to meet the moment" and did not mention fossil fuels, according to the Guardian. The talks dragged on to become the longest climate summit ever, the paper reports, as several nations rejected the "unacceptable deal".

Image caption, The Independent says the COP summit ended in "disarray and disappointment". In a "fraught closing session in Antalya yesterday", countries failed to reach a consensus on a deal, the paper says.

Image caption, New plans to "reform how universal credit works" are being drawn up, The i Paper reports, with the aim to "help people into work". The potential update to the UK's welfare system is "expected to target people claiming health-related benefits" without being on employment support services, the paper says.

Image caption, The Times also leads on disability benefits, saying a review led by UK disability minister Sir Stephen Timms will recommend payments "should be linked to real-life needs and costs". Sir Stephen, who has been looking into disability benefits for the past year, found the system is "no longer fit for purpose", the paper reports.

Image caption, Several newspapers headline on personal revelations from boxer Tyson Fury, who has spoken in a "bombshell documentary" ahead of a major bout with Anthony Joshua next month, according to the Sun. Fury's wife Paris reveals the former heavyweight champion has been "diagnosed with schizophrenia", according to the newspaper.

Image caption, The Daily Mirror says Fury has spoken about the "torment" he suffered after "a series of family traumas". Following his father's imprisonment and wife Paris losing a baby, Fury said: "Words can't explain the darkness I was in," according to the paper.

Image caption, The Daily Star headlines on the Furys' "baby hell" after Paris Fury gave birth to a stillborn son. It also covers Manchester United's loss to Liverpool in its first match under new head coach Mauricio Pochettino.

Image caption, Meanwhile, the Financial Times reports "FTSE 100 catering giant" Compass is planning to move its stock market listing to New York in what the paper says will be a "blow to London". Three quarters of the firm's profits were "generated in North America" last year, according to the paper.

Image caption, The Daily Mail splashes on "five ex-PMs" warning Andy Burnham to not rejoin the EU, including former Tory leaders accusing the prime minister of making an "'utterly shameful' attempt to reopen Brexit wounds", following a deal reached at the UK-EU summit last week.

Image caption, A whistleblower has criticised what she says were Burnham's "empty promises" to victims of sexual abuse, the Daily Express reports. The paper says former detective Maggie Oliver has condemned the prime minister's "failure to act" on an inquiry into institutions that failed children. The Express says it has contacted Burnham for comment.

The front page photo in the Guardian, external captures the anger at the UN climate talks. It shows activists outside the conference in Turkey holding signs saying "shame". The paper's inside analysis says the conference's failure will be measured "not in inches of negotiating text" but in "hopes dashed and hardship endured". The Times, external quotes a negotiator from the Marshall Islands, one of the most vulnerable states to rising sea levels: "We will not compromise our future to benefit fossil fuel interests," they say.

Ahead of the release of a government report into disability benefits tomorrow, the Daily Telegraph, external suggests the prime minister risks "a major rebellion from Labour MPs". The paper says Andy Burnham is preparing to review the eligibility criteria and overall cost of Personal Independence Payments. Separately, the i Paper, external understands that plans are being drawn up to reform Universal Credit for people of all ages, which could open the door to new conditions for claimants. The Department for Work and Pensions says tomorrow's report, by the disability minister, Sir Stephen Timms, and the recently published Milburn Review, will help shape its next steps on welfare reform.

The Daily Mail, external and the Sun, external both point out the list of ex-prime ministers who have warned Andy Burnham against re-opening the Brexit debate. But the Daily Mirror, external says the PM will today "face down his Brexiteer critics" and tell MPs his new reset deal with the EU will "boost the economy by £17bn by 2040".

The Financial Times, external says the FTSE 100 catering giant Compass is planning to move its primary listing to New York, in what the paper calls a "fresh blow to the UK's public markets". The firm has declined to comment.

A few papers carry pictures of the actor Sir Idris Elba walking next to King Charles III. The Mail, external says the two form an "unlikely - and surprisingly moving - double act", in a new Netflix documentary to mark 50 years of the King's Trust. According to the Telegraph, external, Sir Idris said his life could have looked "entirely different" if he'd not received help from the Trust when he was young to train at the National Youth Music Theatre.

If you have been affected by any of the issues raised in this review, information and support can be found at the BBC's Action Line.
